pp:ee:2004:q4.title: GATE EE 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 4
pp:ee:2004:q4.question:
Total instantaneous power supplied by a 3-phase ac supply to a balanced R-L
load is

detailed_solution.concept: Power Systems - Power System Transients
detailed_solution.markdown:
Impedance of the load

$=Z_L=R+j\omega L=|Z|\angle \theta _L$

where, $\theta _L=\tan ^{-1}\left ( \frac{\omega L}{R} \right )$

Voltages of $3-\phi$ supply

$$\begin{aligned}

V_a&=V_m \sin \omega t \\

V_b&=V_m \sin (\omega t-120^{\circ}) \\

V_c &=V_m \sin (\omega t+120^{\circ}) \\

I_a&=\frac{V_a}{Z_L}=\frac{V_m \sin \omega t}{|Z|\angle \theta _L} \\

&= I_M \sin (\omega t-\theta _L)\\

\text{where, } I_m&=\frac{V_m}{|Z|}\\

\text{Similarly,}&\\

I_b&=I_m \sin (\omega t-120-\theta _L)\\

I_c&=I_m \sin (\omega t+120-\theta _L)\\

& \text{Instantaneous power}\\

&=P=V_aI_a+V_bI_b+V_cI_c\\

P&=V_mI_m[\sin \omega t\cdot \sin (\omega t-\theta _L)\\

&+\sin (\omega t-120^{\circ}) \cdot \sin (\omega t-120-\theta _L)\\

&+\sin (\omega t+120^{\circ})\cdot \sin (\omega t+120-\theta _L)]\\

&=\frac{V_mI_m}{2}[(\cos \theta _L -\cos(2\omega t-\theta _L) ) \\

&+(\cos \theta _L -\cos(2\omega t-240-\theta _L) )\\

&+(\cos \theta _L -\cos(2\omega t+240-\theta _L) )]\\

P&=\frac{3V_mI_m}{2}\cos \phi = \text{constant}

\end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2004:q41.title: GATE EE 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 41
pp:ee:2004:q41.question:
The armature resistance of a permanent magnet dc motor is 0.8 $\Omega$. At no load,
the motor draws 1.5 A from a supply voltage of 25 V and runs at 1500 rpm.
The efficiency of the motor while it is operating on load at 1500 rpm drawing a
current of 3.5 A from the same source will be

detailed_solution.concept: Electrical Machines - DC Machines
detailed_solution.markdown: At no load, $$\begin{aligned} I_{a0} &= 1.5A\\ \text{supply voltage} &= V_t=250V\\ &\text{Back emf at no load,}\\ E_{b0}&=V_t-I_{a0}R_a \\ &= 25-1.5 \times 0.8\\ &= 23.8V\\ &\text{Power developed by the motor} \\ P_0=E_{b0}I_{a0} &=23.8 \times 1.5 \\ &= 35.7 W \end{aligned}$$ As the motor is working at no load, power $P_0$ supplies no load losses. When the motor is on load, $$\begin{aligned} I_{a1} &= 3.5A\\ E_{a1}&=V_t-I_{a1}R_a \\ &= 25-3.5 \times 0.8\\ &= 22.2V\\ &\text{Power developed by the motor} \\ P_1=E_{a1}I_{a1} &=22.2 \times 3.5 \\ &= 77.7 W\\ &\text{Power available at shaft}\\ P_s&=P_1-\text{no load losses}\\ &=77.7-35.7=42W\\ \text{Efficiency}&=\frac{\text{Output power}}{input power} \times 100\\ &=\frac{P_0}{V_tT_{a_1}} \times 100\\ &=\frac{42}{25 \times 3.5} \times 100=48\% \end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2004:q44.title: GATE EE 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 44
pp:ee:2004:q44.question:
A single-phase, 230 V, 50 Hz, 4-pole, capacitor-start induction motor had the following stand-still impedances.

Main winding $Z_{m} = 6.0 + j4.0 \Omega$

primary.subtopicLabel: Single Phase Induction Motors, Special Purpose Machines and Electromechanical Energy Conversion System

detailed_solution.concept: Electrical Machines - Single Phase Induction Motors, Special Purpose Machines and Electromechanical Energy Conversion System
detailed_solution.markdown: Supply voltage V is taken as reference. Current in main winding $I_m=\frac{V}{Z_m}$ $\Rightarrow \; I_m=\frac{230\angle 0^{\circ}}{6+j4}=31.89\angle -33.7^{\circ}$ Staring capacitor (C) wil be connected in series with the auxilary winding, so modified auxiliary winding impedance. $$\begin{aligned} Z_m &= 8+j6-\frac{j}{\omega C}\\ &= 8+j\left ( 6-\frac{1}{\omega C} \right )\\ &= 8-j\left ( \frac{1}{\omega C}-6 \right ) \end{aligned}$$ Current in auxiliary winding, $$\begin{aligned} I_a &=\frac{V}{Z_a} \\ &= \frac{230\angle 0^{\circ}}{8-j\left ( \frac{1}{\omega C}-6 \right )}\\ &=|I_a|\angle \tan^{-1}\left ( \frac{\frac{1}{\omega C}-6 }{8} \right ) \end{aligned}$$ Capacitor is provided to make angle between $I_a$ and $I_m90^{\circ}.$ $$\begin{aligned} \text{So,}\;\; \angle I_m+\angle I_a&=90^{\circ} \\ \angle I_a&= 90^{\circ}-33.7^{\circ}=56.3^{\circ}\\ \tan^{-1}\left ( \frac{\frac{1}{\omega C}-6 }{8} \right )&= 56.3^{\circ}\\ \frac{1}{\omega C} &= 18\\ \omega &= 2 \pi f=2 \pi \times 50 \text{rad/sec} \\ C&=176.84\mu F \end{aligned}$$

pp:ee:2004:q59.title: GATE EE 2004 | Set 1 | Question: 59
pp:ee:2004:q59.question:
A 50 Hz, 4-pole, 500 MVA, 22 kV turbo-generator is delivering rated megavoltamperes
at 0.8 power factor. Suddenly a fault occurs reducing in electric power
output by 40%. Neglect losses and assume constant power input to the shaft.
The accelerating torque in the generator in MNm at the time of fault will be

detailed_solution.concept: Power Systems - Power System Stability
detailed_solution.markdown:
Before fault, mechanical input $(P_m)=$ Electrical output $(P_e)$

$= 500 \times 0.8=400MW$

After fault, mechanical input remains same $=P_m=400MW$

While electrical output reduces by 40 %.

So, electrical output at the time of fault

$=(P_e)_f= 0.6 \times 400 =240MW$

Accelerating power $=P_a=P_m-(P_e)_f$

$=400-240=160MW$

Synchronous speed (in rpm)

$N_s=\frac{120 \times f}{P}=\frac{120 \times 50}{4}=1500\; rpm$

Synchronous speed (in rad/sec)

$\omega _s=\frac{2 \pi N_s}{60}=\frac{2 \pi \times 1500}{60}=157 \text{ rad/sec}$

$P_a=T_a\omega$

$\Rightarrow \;T_a\omega$ (accelerating Torque)

$=\frac{P_a}{\omega _s}=\frac{160}{157}MN-m=1.018MN-m$
